character: the regime's bunker plate, riveted by the lowest bidder: it dents like a biscuit tin, tears along its rivet lines with the torn edge curling out at you, and the rivets pop off like buttons off a general's coat. A beam melts a kerf that cools white, orange, red, then a blue-straw temper tint.
hash: h32 as concrete (tools/art_host/fx/hashrule.py); salt 202 torn, 203 cut

strips.layout: column = variant v, row = pair p = ia * 4 + ib (ia, ib = the level index of the start / end vertex)
column = variant v, row = pair p = ia * 4 + ib (ia, ib = the level index of the start / end vertex)

stages.use: columns = variants (h32(cx, cy, 71 + salt) % 4), rows = stages 25 / 50 / 75 % of dmg / threshold, cumulative. Centre the 48 px canvas on the cell and draw it over the neighbours clipped to steel matter: creases cross the cell border. 25: dents and scratches; 50: + a buckle crease, a popped rivet socket; 75: + a torn seam, two sockets (spawn a flying rivet per socket).

chips.use: one per pellet, anchor on the hit pixel, variant h32(x, y, 80 + salt) % 6; spawn 2-3 sliver fragments + sparks

rows: flying head, 4 frames at 24 fps, loop while airborne
rivets.use: a stage 50 / 75 socket or a torn edge passing a rivet: the head pops out at 3-6 cells/s up and away, spins, lands, lies 1 s

ramp.columns: px into the matter from the cut edge (0 = the edge pixel)

drips.use: on the LOWER lip of a beam cut (matter above the kerf edge is the upper lip; drips hang from the lower edge of the UPPER lip): one drip every 5 + h32 % 9 px during steps 0-1, frames at 12 fps, frame 3 falls at 6 cells/s and dies on the first matter

hot.coldBreakup: the cold row is drawn only where h32(x, y, 88 + salt) % 4 != 0 (d 0) / % 2 == 0 (d 1): a tint, not an outline
hot.path: the beam removed cells must be 4-connected (a supercover line: at each diagonal step add the cell on the inside of the turn), or the kerf breaks into separate slots
hot.use: a cell removed by a BEAM (the plasma / laser weapons): its edge uses cutEdges, then for each matter pixel within 4 px of the kerf (4-connected distance d, 0 = touching the hole) draw ramp[step][d] over the art (additive glow on top is the render side's; these colours are opaque). step = 0 / 1 / 2 / cold by the ms since that pixel was cut. A shader: one distance field from the kerf + this 4 x 4 lookup. The light the glow throws (a warm point light along the cut for 0-300 ms) is the render side's.

facets.#00ff00: the plate face, cut from the cell art

chunks.use: as concrete (chunks.use): 2-5 a removed cell; slivers 0-1 fly first with sparks; steel scrap does not pile high: repose 28 deg

facets.#00ff00: the wall's painted face kept AS IT IS (it reads as a piece of this wall)
facets.#ff0000: the broken top edge: the section, lit

slabs.use: holes of 3+ cells: min(4, 1 + n // 2) slabs, cut from removed cell (i * 3) % n at hashed offsets (keys 64-66), leaning on the wall foot by a shear of one px every 2-3 rows (alternate sides), 1 in 3 stood on end; then the chunks on a 36 deg cone within +-min(32, 10 + 6n) px of the hole centre; grains at the toe

section: a plate is 2 px thick: in a torn hole the lower lip shows its cut top RAMP[4] then RAMP[3]; the upper lip's underside RAMP[0]; the sides RAMP[2]
rim: torn (blast / shot): the matter beside the hole CURLS OUT: 1 px RAMP[4] at the edge facing up / left, a second px RAMP[3] behind it on up-facing edges, RAMP[0] on down / right edges, 1 rust px in 6

kerf.ref: tools/art_host/fx/hole_assemble.py kerf_mask(shape, x0, y0, x1, y1, 11, salt 203)
kerf.use: a beam cut is drawn along the REAL line of the beam (any angle): the sim removes the cells the line passes; the picture is the kerf over them (matter outside the kerf stays drawn). cutEdges is the grid fallback for a renderer without a fine mask.
